data.title: Surf PRC Plot Data Gets Cut Off in DateTime Mode
data.repro_steps: PAD & Well (18th May) When navigating to the Surf PRC plot, the plot renders correctly initially, but data gets cut off when viewed in DateTime mode. The issue impacts visibility of complete data points and affects plot readability. Steps to Reproduce: Open Live+ / Surf PRC plot. Switch the X-axis mode to DateTime . Observe the plotted data range. Actual Result: Data appears truncated/cut off in DateTime mode. Expected Result: All plot data should render completely without truncation in DateTime mode.

data.title: Real-Time Plot UI Does Not Refresh Despite GetDataChart Receiving New Data
data.repro_steps: When opening the plot in Real Time mode, the GetDataChart API continuously receives new data (approximately 5 seconds worth of data per API call), but the plot in the UI does not refresh automatically. The latest data only becomes visible after performing a hard browser refresh. Steps to Reproduce: Open the plot in Real Time mode. Monitor the GetDataChart API response in Network tab. Observe that new data is returned in every API call. Check the plot behavior in the UI. Actual Result: The UI plot does not refresh/update automatically even though new data is being received from the API. Expected Result: The plot should automatically refresh and display the latest incoming data in real time without requiring a hard refresh.

data.title: FracPro- Live+ real-time plot does not auto-refresh despite receiving MQTT data via GetDataChart API
data.repro_steps: Description The real-time plot in Live+ QA does not auto-refresh/update when live MQTT data is being streamed. The stage is confirmed as live (green indicator). The GetDataChart API is successfully returning data (verified via browser DevTools Network tab), but the plot UI does not reflect the incoming data. The same plot in LiveX auto-refreshes correctly under identical conditions. Steps to reproduce Open Live+ QA at liveplus-qa.linqx.io Navigate to Results → Plot for a pad/well with an active live stage (green indicator) Confirm MQTT data is streaming (stage shows live/green) Observe the real-time plot — it does not update automatically Open the same plot in LiveX and confirm it auto-refreshes correctly Inspect the Network tab in DevTools — confirm GetDataChart returns data with success: true and realtimeData populated Expected behavior The real-time plot in Live+ should automatically refresh and render incoming MQTT data , consistent with LiveX behavior. Actual behavior The plot remains static. Data is returned by the API but the chart component does not re-render or update with new values. Evidence / Attachments Screenshot attached showing DevTools Network panel with GetDataChart returning realtimeData with multiple timestamped entries ( 2026-06-01T16:00:49Z onwards) while the plot remains unchanged.

data.title: Plot Channel Color Does Not Use Default Color Configured in Settings
data.repro_steps: The application is not applying the default channel color configured in the Settings page when a user selects a channel while creating or editing a plot. For example, in the ProFrac Settings page, Treating Pressure is configured with the color Red . When a ProFrac user selects Treating Pressure from the Real-Time Channel list in the Plot page, the selected channel should automatically display in Red. However, the application assigns a random color instead of using the configured color. This issue is observed for both: Real-Time Channels FracPro Channels Expected Behavior: When a channel has a color configured in the Settings page, the same color should be automatically applied when the channel is added to a plot. The system should use the configured default color rather than assigning a random color. This behavior should be consistent for both Real-Time and FracPro channels. Actual Behavior: A random color is assigned when the channel is selected in the plot, even though a default color is configured in Settings. Steps to Reproduce: Navigate to Settings and configure a color for a channel (e.g., Treating Pressure = Red). Save the settings. Navigate to the Plot page. Create a new plot or edit an existing plot. Select the configured channel from the Real-Time Channel or FracPro Channel list. Observe the assigned color. Result: The channel is assigned a random color. Expected Result: The channel should be assigned the color configured in Settings (e.g., Red for Treating Pressure).

data.title: Plot Screen - Marker Can Be Dragged Using Keyboard Without Proper Grab/Selection After Zoom or Key Release
data.repro_steps: Description Users are able to move/drag plot markers using keyboard arrow keys even when the marker is not actively grabbed or selected. Additionally, after releasing the keyboard key, marker movement functionality remains active, allowing further dragging actions without reselecting the marker. The issue is also reproducible after performing a zoom operation on the plot. This behavior can result in unintended marker position changes and inaccurate data adjustments. Preconditions User is logged into the application. Plot screen is loaded with draggable markers. Marker manipulation through keyboard controls is enabled. Steps to Reproduce Scenario 1: Dragging After Key Release Navigate to the Plot screen. Select and grab a marker. Press and hold the keyboard arrow key to move the marker. Release the keyboard key. Attempt to continue dragging or moving the marker using keyboard inputs without re-grabbing the marker. Scenario 2: Dragging After Zoom Navigate to the Plot screen. Perform a zoom-in or zoom-out operation. Without explicitly grabbing the marker, press keyboard arrow keys. Observe marker behavior. Scenario 3: Slow Increment Drag Validation Navigate to the Plot screen. Grab a marker. Move the marker using keyboard keys in small increments. Release the marker. Press keyboard keys again without selecting the marker. Actual Result Marker continues to respond to keyboard drag actions even after the key has been released. After zooming, markers can be moved using keyboard keys without first grabbing/selecting the marker. Marker focus/state is not properly reset after key release or zoom operations. Expected Result Marker movement should only occur when the marker is actively grabbed/selected. Once the keyboard key is released, marker movement should stop immediately. After zoom operations, users should be required to explicitly grab/select the marker before any keyboard-based movement is allowed. Marker focus and drag state should be cleared appropriately after drag completion.

data.title: Channel Settings - Dropdown List Overlaps and Appears Behind Lower Sections When Adding/Editing a Channel
data.repro_steps: Description When a user navigates to Channel Settings and attempts to add or edit a channel, the dropdown menu does not display correctly. Instead of appearing above all page elements, the dropdown extends underneath the section below, causing some options to be partially or completely hidden. This indicates a possible z-index, layering, or container overflow issue affecting the dropdown component. Preconditions User is logged into the application. User has access to Channel Settings. At least one configurable channel is available. Steps to Reproduce Navigate to Channel Settings . Click Add Channel or edit an existing channel. Open any dropdown field within the channel configuration. Observe the dropdown list. Actual Result The dropdown menu is rendered behind or underneath the section below. Some dropdown options are hidden or not fully visible. Users may be unable to select all available options. Expected Result The dropdown should be displayed above all underlying page sections. All dropdown options should be fully visible and accessible. The dropdown should not be clipped, overlapped, or hidden by surrounding containers.

data.title: FracPro Live X - FIX  Error Messages from Dashboard in Live X
data.repro_steps: When navigating to the Dashboard page in the Stage environment, the page displays error notifications: "Oops! Something went wrong. Please contact us for support." "Unexpected token '<', '<!doctype...' is not valid JSON" The error indicates that the frontend expects a JSON response but is receiving an HTML document instead, causing JSON parsing to fail and preventing the dashboard data from loading. Preconditions User is logged into Stage environment. Access to Dashboard module. Steps to Reproduce Login to stage.fracpro.ai . Navigate to Dashboard . Observe the page load behavior. Check the notification area and browser Network tab. 106765. Actual Result Dashboard displays error notifications: "Oops! Something went wrong. Please contact us for support." "Unexpected token '<', '<!doctype...' is not valid JSON" Dashboard content does not load correctly. Expected Result Dashboard should load successfully without any error notifications. APIs should return valid JSON responses. Realtime Treatment and Well data should be displayed correctly.

data.title: GetDataChart API Calls Increase on Every Dashboard Navigation Causing Duplicate Requests
data.repro_steps: Steps to Reproduce: Navigate to Well A → Stage 1 . Run the model and open the Network tab. Verify that the GetDataChart API is called once for model time updates. Navigate to the Dashboard screen. Return to Well A → Stage 1 . Observe the number of GetDataChart API calls in the Network tab. Repeat the navigation sequence ( Dashboard → Well A Stage 1 ) multiple times. Expected Result: Only a single active GetDataChart API request/subscription should exist for the current well and stage regardless of navigation. Returning to the same stage should not create additional API calls. Actual Result: Each time the user navigates to the Dashboard and returns to the same well/stage, an additional GetDataChart API call is created: Initial load: 1 call After first return: 2 calls After second return: 3 calls Continues increasing with each navigation cycle

data.title: Multiple Calls Generated for Treatment API on Dashboard and Treatment Schedule Screens
data.repro_steps: Steps to Reproduce: Navigate to a well. Open the Treatment Schedule screen. Open the browser Network tab. Monitor the API: /api/v1/tokens/auth/wells/36459/treatments/75178 Navigate between Dashboard and Treatment Schedule screens multiple times. Observe the number of API calls generated for the treatment endpoint. data.title: MinifracParam GET API - Remove Epoch Timestamp & treatment id from API Endpoint URL
data.repro_steps: The MinifracParam GET API request is currently appending an epoch timestamp & treatment id to the API endpoint URL (e.g., minifracParams?_=1782394643900&treatmentId=117591 ). The timestamp is unnecessary and should be removed from the API request to keep the endpoint clean and consistent. Steps to Reproduce Open the application. Navigate to the Minifrac module. Open the browser Developer Tools (F12) . Go to the Network tab. Trigger the MinifracParam GET API request. Observe the API request URL in the Network tab. Actual Result The MinifracParam GET API endpoint includes an appended epoch timestamp parameter (highlighted in the screenshot). Example: minifracParams?_=1782394643900&treatmentId=117591 Expected Result The MinifracParam GET API should not append an epoch timestamp parameter to the request URL. The API endpoint should be called without the unnecessary timestamp.

data.title: Step Length Bar Disappears After Editing Step Length in Measured Data and Subsequently in Surf PRC Plot
data.repro_steps: Module Results → Plot (Measured Data / Surf PRC) Environment Live+ Stage Preconditions User is logged into Live+ Stage. well( BFM G310H ) with Measured Data and Surf PRC plots is available. Steps to Reproduce Open the desired well. Navigate to Results → Plot . Open the Measured Data plot. Enable the Step Length bar. Modify any step length by dragging its boundary. Release the mouse and observe the Step Length bar. Navigate to the Surf PRC plot. Enable the Step Length bar (if not already enabled). Modify any step length by dragging its boundary. Release the mouse and observe the Step Length bar. Actual Result In the Measured Data plot, the Step Length bar disappears immediately after the user modifies a step length and releases the mouse. After navigating to the Surf PRC plot, the same behavior occurs. The Step Length bar again disappears after editing a step length. The user must repeatedly re-enable the Step Length bar to continue making edits. Expected Result The Step Length bar should remain visible after modifying a step length in both Measured Data and Surf PRC plots. Its visibility should persist throughout the editing session and while navigating between plots.

data.title: Horizontal scrollbar in Fluid List disappears when scrolled back to the left( Material Selection > Add new Fluid List)
data.repro_steps: Description The Fluid List table has the first three columns fixed, while the remaining columns are horizontally scrollable. However, the horizontal scrollbar behaves incorrectly: After scrolling completely back to the left, the horizontal scrollbar disappears , preventing users from scrolling again unless they click at the bottom. This results in poor usability and makes navigating the table difficult. Preconditions User is logged into the application. Navigate to the Material Selection > Fluid List page. The table contains enough columns to require horizontal scrolling. Steps to Reproduce Open the Fluid List page. Observe that the first three columns are fixed. Scroll horizontally to the right. Scroll back completely to the left. Observe the behavior of the horizontal scrollbar. Actual Result After scrolling back to the extreme left, the horizontal scrollbar disappears. Expected Result The scrollbar should remain visible and functional regardless of the current horizontal scroll position. Returning to the left-most position should not cause the scrollbar to disappear.

data.title: Incorrect X-axis values sent in command when adding pressure on SQRT and Log-Log plots
data.repro_steps: Description: When a user adds pressure on the SQRT or Log-Log plot, the Command API sends the raw X value in the request payload instead of the transformed value. For the SQRT plot, the X value should be converted to its square root, and for the Log-Log plot, it should be converted to its logarithmic value before being sent. Steps to Reproduce: Open the FracPro LIVE+ application and navigate to the MiniFrac Analysis section. Open either the SQRT plot or the Log-Log plot. Open the browser Network tab to monitor the Command API request. Right-click on the plot and select Add Pressure. Click Yes to confirm the action. Inspect the payload of the Command API request. Observe the value sent for the X coordinate. Actual Result: The Command API sends the raw X value in the payload for both the SQRT and Log-Log plots without applying the required transformation. Expected Result: The Command API payload should send: SQRT Plot: The square root of the X value for the selected point, while the Y value should remain unchanged. Log-Log Plot: The logarithmic (log) value of the X coordinate for the selected point, same for Y value.

data.title: Chemical Unit Selection Is Not Persisted After Save in Material Selection
data.repro_steps: Users are unable to save the selected Unit for a Chemical in the Material Selection screen. Although the user selects a unit and clicks Save , the updated Unit is not persisted. Upon refresh or reopening the screen, the Unit reverts to its previous/default value. This prevents users from successfully updating the Chemical Unit. Preconditions User is logged into Live+. User has access to the Material Selection screen. At least one Chemical record exists. Steps to Reproduce Navigate to Material Selection . Open the Chemical tab. Select an existing Chemical. Change the Unit to a different value. Click Save . Refresh the screen or reopen the Material Selection page. Actual Result The selected Unit is not saved. The Unit reverts to its previous/default value after saving or refreshing. Expected Result The selected Unit should be successfully saved. The updated Unit should persist after saving and remain unchanged after refreshing or reopening the screen.

data.title: Wellbore Configuration – First digit entered in OD, ID, and Weight fields is not captured on initial keystroke
data.repro_steps: Environment Application: FracPro Live+ Module: Wellbore Configuration Tab: Casing Preconditions User is logged into the application. A well is available with access to the Wellbore Configuration module. Steps to Reproduce Navigate to Wellbore Configuration . Open the Casing tab. Click on any editable field in the OD , ID , or Weight column. Type a numeric value (e.g., 123 ). Actual Result The first digit entered is not recognized After entering second time values is accepted (e.g., typing 123 ) Users must re-enter the first digit to achieve the intended value. Expected Result The application should capture and display every digit entered , including the first keystroke , immediately after the field receives focus.

data.title: Treatment Schedule Design – Save button remains disabled after pasting value into Step Alias column
data.repro_steps: Environment Application: FracPro Live+ Module: Treatment Schedule Design Preconditions User has to edit schedule in treatment schedule design Steps to Reproduce Navigate to Treatment Schedule Design . Click on Edit schedule Locate the Step Alias column. Copy a valid value. Paste the copied value into a Step Alias cell. Observe the Save button. Actual Result The pasted value is displayed in the Step Alias field. However, the Save button remains disabled , preventing the user from saving the changes. Expected Result After a value is pasted into the Step Alias field, the application should recognize the modification as a valid change. The Save button should become enabled , allowing the user to save the updated Treatment Schedule.
